source.paraphrase: New TypeScript speaks @solana/kit v8 with plugins; web3.js v1 stays only inside one legacy adapter.

invariants.why: web3.js v1 is legacy: unmodular, un-tree-shakeable, and its idioms teach the agent 2023 code.
invariants.fixHint: Use @solana/kit with plugins (createClient().use(...)). If legacy code remains, isolate it in one adapter module instead of importing it everywhere.
invariants.avoid: Re-exporting web3.js from a shared barrel so every module keeps importing it.

source.paraphrase: Wallet UI goes through Wallet Standard or an embedded wallet, not the legacy adapter packages.

invariants.why: The old wallet-adapter packages pull the legacy stack back in and bypass Wallet Standard.
invariants.fixHint: Use @solana/kit-plugin-wallet with @solana/react (Wallet Standard), or Privy for embedded wallets.
invariants.avoid: Wrapping the old adapter in a hook and calling that the new wallet layer.

source.paraphrase: Anchor programs pair with the client package of their own line, and one repo pins one line.

invariants.why: Anchor 1.x moved the TypeScript client to @anchor-lang/core; the old package pins the repo to the 0.32 line.
invariants.fixHint: Import from @anchor-lang/core and pin one Anchor line per repo from Anchor.toml. Prefer a Codama-generated client from the IDL over hand-written calls.
invariants.avoid: Aliasing the old package to the new name so both lines coexist.

source.paraphrase: Kit examples build token instructions with @solana-program/token and @solana-program/token-2022; @solana/spl-token appears only in the Legacy examples next to web3.js v1, which it requires as a peer dependency.

invariants.why: @solana/spl-token takes and returns web3.js v1 PublicKey and Transaction objects, so importing it pulls the legacy client back into a Kit codebase even when web3.js itself is never imported.
invariants.fixHint: Use the Codama-generated program clients: @solana-program/token for the Token program and @solana-program/token-2022 for Token Extensions.
invariants.avoid: Barrel re-exports, require() and deep subpath imports load the same package. Mentions in comments or plain strings are not matched.
